steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan (see Cook's Note).
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl; set aside.

Beat butter and sugar together in a separate large bowl with an electric mixer until noticeably lighter in color and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, allowing each egg to blend into the beaten butter mixture before adding the next. Mix in coconut extract.
Pour in flour mixture alternately with buttermilk, mixing until just incorporated. Fold in coconut, mixing just enough to evenly combine. Pour cake batter into prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean, about 1 hour.
If desired, frost cooled cake with your favorite buttercream frosting and sprinkle with flaked coconut.

raw_recipe.headline: Moist Coconut Cake
raw_recipe.description: This coconut cake recipe makes a soft and moist cake with easy baking ingredients, coconut extract, and flaked coconut for a great coconut flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Moist Coconut Cake

review.reviewBody: A great, moist coconut cake, it made a big hit at work. I read member comments and modified the original by reducing sugar to 1 1/2 cups, and also added a box of vanilla instant pudding, 1 tspn of vanilla extract (in addition to the coconut), 1 tspn of baking soda, and a small can of (drained) crushed pineapple. It was done in 50 minutes, and came out of the pan perfectly. I glazed it with warmed (microwaved) cream cheese packaged icing, then topped it with coconut flakes. Yummy!

Great recipe, and like most people commenting, the cake went quick. I made this with a few alterations being most of the family is gluten free. I used Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free flour in lieu of all-purpose. The other alterations are, 3/4 tsp baking powder, 3/4 + tsp baking soda, 1.5 cups of white sugar & 4 large eggs. I baked in (2) 9" baking rounds and made a cream cheese frosting to layer & cover. I then added shredded coconut to the frosting. It was dense, but delicious.
Thanks for the recipe and the various alteration comments made. It all has to start somewhere.

Fantastic! After reading the reviews, I cut the sugar to 1.5 cups and it was just right. I baked it in three layer cake pans (lined the bottom with waxed paper, greased/floured sides) and had no problem getting them out of the pans. I used the Butter Cream Coconut frosting from this site (minus the pecans, since it was for Easter) and it was devoured.

With a few changes, reading other reviews and following strict directions this cake is AMAZING!!! Be sure that are required ingredients are at room temperature; just 4 eggs were enough; I made my own buttermilk by putting white vinegar in milk; sift in a box of cream of coconut pudding with your dry ingredients (yes there are little bits of coconut flakes that can just be tossed in after sifting); I used cake flour; and 40 -45 minutes for me gave a clean toothpick. I also used a cream cheese frosting and pineapple filling that I made by cooking a can of crushed pineapples (with the juice), 2 TBSP of cornstarch and 1cup of sugar for about 6 minutes while stirring regularly, after it cooled I used it on the middle layer, frosted the top with cream cheese frosting and dusted with coconut while leaving the sides bare. DELICIOUS!!!

I thought this was a wonderful moist cake. I iced it with coconut butter cream and added sweetened coconut to the outside. I served it for Valentine's Day at a dinner party I gave and it was a BIG hit! I will be keeping this recipe and definitely making it again. I do recommend cutting parchment paper and lining the pan. It makes it so easy to remove.

I was intrigued by the reviews and wanted to test for myself. As usual, I average out what previous reviews say, so for this recipe, used bit less sugar, half an egg less, and used 1 tsp baking soda in place of 1 of the tsps of baking powder. Used vanilla extract instead of coconut and I also used half buttermilk, half pineapple juice. Along with a pineapple buttercream frosting this was DELICIOUS. Nice and sweet, definitely satisfied the craving for a sweet cake. I am the only one in the house that likes coconut, so this cake is ALL MINE.. Muahaha.

I made the cake as written, but I did not use the icing. I don't like all butter frosting. I used frozen coconut and also added aboit 1 teaspoon additional coconut flavoring in the frosting and did not include pecans or other nuts. I toasted coconut to place on top. This cake was sold in a bake sale for $40. I wanted to sit down with a fork and eat it all by myself!!!

Tasty! this has a moist but very dense poundcake like texture. I followed the recipe exactly minus half cup sugar and since I used two 7.75" oval Wilton pans it only needed 45mins at 325 deg. Personally next time I'd reduce the sugar a bit more because frosting would make it too sweet for my taste. The secret is to have the butter VERY room temp and creaming it with sugar for a long 5minutes, scraping the bowl in between.

I made this cake and use recommendations of other reviewers. I used 2 9"pans instead of the 10" the recipe called for. Adjust your cooking time down to 40-45 minutes. I also added 1 pkg of coconut instant pudding and added 1/2 cup of coconut milk to the recipe. Finally, I used a processor to shred the coconut just a bit further. The batter is thicker than usual but it works. It came out with a nice subtle coconut flavor & moist. I have a Kitchen Aide mixer so that always shortens the prep time.

I don't usually follow changes made by other bakers until I've followed the recipe exactly, but 2 cups of sugar to 2 cups of flour seemed a bit much. I'm glad I did (only use 1 1/2 cups sugar). Cake was perfectly moist, not too sweet and even without the coconut extract (didn't have it; used vanilla), very coconutty. Watch the baking time; mine baked in 45 minutes. Definitely making this again!

For those of you whose cake didn't rise, make sure all of your ingredients are room temperature (take it out the night before), make sure you beat the butter and sugar for at least 5 minutes, and fold in the coconut. Technique is everything with this cake. You might also want to check that your baking powder is fresh. This is a solid recipe.

My rating is with these changes. After taking other reviews into consideration and a few alterations of my own, I think these substitutions make the best cake: 4 eggs, 1-1/4 cup sugar, 1 tbsp coconut extract, 2 cups coconut, apple sauce instead of butter, coconut milk instead of buttermilk, 3/4 tsp baking soda, 3/4 tsp baking powder, Chop coconut in hand blender. Best if made in 2 layers. For frosting: make pudding and set aside, seperately melt dark chocolate with remainder of coconut milk. When cool, add pudding mix (just powder). Mix this mixture into pudding. Or: Beat cream of coconut with cool whip and pour over cake. Cover with shredded coconut.

this was a great cake. Real easy to make, great flavor, very moist and delicious tasty I did reduce the sugar from 2 cups to a cup and a half., I used all five eggs and I added 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. I also used unsweetened coconut for the outside and I toasted it. It was great. My family loved it.
I love this situation much it is so delicious and everything you need is right at the top thank you so much this is the most delicious cake I have ever had

This is by far my favorite coconut cake recipe. I always get rave reviews. I altered the recipe slightly by adding a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the batter and I decreased the sugar to 1 and 3/4 cups. I will be adding it to my repotoire of cakes!
Super easy to make. Moist and favored just right. Perfect
I frosted it with a coconut Grenache receipt I have which is chocolate. Delicious!
Great recipe, truly moist and delicious! Used the exact recipe. I filled the cake with a thin layer of cherry jam and drizzled coconut flavored sugar glaze on top instead of the buttercream frosting.
My husband wanted a coconut cake. First time making from scratch too...
This was very easy for my grandtwins to help me. 5 eggs means extra protein and super moist. I used whole milk, and vanilla for the best vanilla cake I have ever tasted.
No changes.
